Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:73: And let us conclude this Gate with the virtue of the penitent. They said in Vayikra Rabbah (7:2), in these words: from where do we learn that for one who performs repentance, it is accounted to him as though he had gone up to Jerusalem, built the Temple and the altar, and offered upon it all the sacrifices of the Torah? As it is said (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:74: Further, they said in Midrash Tehillim (Psalm 18 [sic]), on the psalm "upon Shoshannim, of the sons of Korach" (Psalms 45:1), in these words: whoever performs repentance from a transgression in his hand, the Holy One, blessed be He, adds and calls him by a beloved name. Come and see with the sons of Korach - before they repented, they were not called "lilies" [shoshanim] and "beloved" [yedidim]; once they repented, they were called "lilies" and "beloved," as it is said, "upon Shoshannim, a maskil, a song of loves" [yedidot]. And so David - before he repented he was not written in the register above; once he repented, he was written in the register above, and called "servant," as it is said (Psalms 18:1), "to the chief musician, of the servant of the LORD, of David" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:75: Further, on the virtue of repentance, it is explained in the Yerushalmi (Ta'anit, chapter 4): it is written (Joel 2:13), "and rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn to the LORD your God, for He is gracious and merciful." Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, if you rend your heart in repentance, you need not rend your garments - neither for your sons nor for your daughters, but for the LORD your God. Why? "For He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and relents from the evil" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 7:76: With this this Gate is concluded, in Nun-Lamed-Kaf and Ayin-Vav-Yud [sealing acronym]. May the Name grant us the merit to be among those who perform complete repentance before Him, with love and fear - so may it be His will, Amen, Selah and forever.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:1: Concerning the matter of holiness, we were commanded several times in the Torah. The first, at the end of Parashat Shemini (Leviticus 11:44), "sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am holy," and so on. And in Parashat Kedoshim it is mentioned three times: the first, at the beginning of the parashah (ibid. 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy"; and afterward (ibid. 20:7), "sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am the LORD your God"; and at the end of the parashah (ibid. 20:26), "and you shall be holy to Me, for I the LORD am holy, and have set you apart from the peoples, that you should be Mine." And in the passage of tzitzit (Numbers 15:40), "that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy to your God." Further, in Parashat Emor El HaKohanim (Leviticus 22:32), "neither shall you profane My holy Name, but I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" - and this is a positive commandment to sanctify His Name publicly, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:2: And since this statement, "you shall be holy," appears in the Torah so many times, even though it is not among the essential 248 commandments, nevertheless it is a root for performing all the commandments for the sake of the One who commands them - for once a person is holy and separated from the affairs of love of this world, he will strive to do his Owner's will truly, and bind himself in love of Him, blessed be He, to perform His commandments with desire and love, for what does he have to do with this world and its goods - as will be explained, with God's help, what the ways of holiness are. And therefore it is doubled in the Torah so many times, because of the abundant benefit that follows from this for the soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:3: A reason for the nature of holiness, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Tanchuma (beginning of Parashat Kedoshim), in these words: this is what Scripture says (Isaiah 5:16), "but the LORD of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and God the Holy shall be sanctified in righteousness" - He sanctifies Himself in His world through righteousness, meaning that He teaches an advocacy for Israel, as it is said (ibid. 63:1), "I who speak in righteousness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:4: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, in the future I shall be sanctified through you, as it is said (ibid. 29:23), "for when he sees his children," and so on, and so it says of Israel (ibid. 49:3), "in whom I will be glorified." You are sanctified through Me, and I am sanctified through you, as it is said (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:5: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: before I created you, the ministering angels would praise and sanctify Me through you, saying, "blessed be the LORD, God of Israel, from world to world" (Psalms 106:48). Once Adam, the first man, was created, they said, this is he through whose name we praise You - He said to them, this one is a thief, as it is said (Genesis 3:17), "and you have eaten of the tree," and so on. Noah came; they said to Him, this is he - He said to them, this one is a drunkard, as it is said (ibid. 9:21), "and he drank of the wine." Abraham came; they said to Him, this is he - He said to them, this one is a convert [not from birth]. Isaac came; they said to Him, this is he - He said to them, this one loves the one who hates Me [Esau]. Jacob came; they said to Him, this is he - He said to them, yes - and so it says (ibid. 35:10), "your name shall no more be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name" - and all of Israel is called by his name. At that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctified Israel to His Name, as it is said (Isaiah 49:3), "Israel, in whom I will be glorified."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:6: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: since you were sanctified to My Name before I created the world, be holy as I am holy, as it is said, "you shall be holy, for I am holy." A parable: to what may this be compared? To a king who betrothed a woman; he said to her, since you have been sanctified [betrothed] to my name, I am king and you are queen; just as this is My honor, so is it your honor, since you are my wife. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, sanctify the people to Me, as it is said (Exodus 19:10), "go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow" - sanctify them. The Holy One, blessed be He, came and said to them (ibid. 19:6), "and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation." Why? "For I the LORD am holy" - you too shall be holy, since I have sanctified you to My Name, as it is said, "speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say to them, you shall be holy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:7: And although this discourse is deep, and contains several precise points every reader must scrutinize, nevertheless we have not come, in this composition, to explain anything but what pertains to practical matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:8: In what the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "you are sanctified through Me, and I am sanctified through you" - the matter is that first we are sanctified through Him, drawing holiness from Him to us, so that we be sanctified through the performance of the commandments, and afterward He is sanctified through us, through the arousal from below that ascends from our deeds. And the reason is that all things require arousal from below, as explained several times, and it will be further explained below in the discourse "may He send your help from the sanctuary."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:9: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, "before I created you," and so on - now he comes to give a reason for how Israel can reach such a supernal level and draw from the secret of the supernal holiness, for on the surface they have no grip above. For this he gave a reason concerning the matter of the angels, who would praise the Holy One, blessed be He, before man was created, saying "God of Israel," and when Jacob came, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, this is Israel. And the matter is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 24a), the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Mishpatim, page 119a), and the Tikkunim (page 102a): the secret of "Israel" arose in thought, and this is the secret of the son drawn from the brain of Abba - and from this reality is the root of the souls of Israel, and Jacob was their root in his supernal reality called "Israel." And although we say (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God," the intent is that when the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah unite, they draw the souls from above, from the brain of Abba and Imma - and it follows, according to this, that the source of souls is from the place of holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:10: And what he said, "at that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctified Israel to His Name, as it is said, 'Israel, in whom I will be glorified'" - the intent is that the souls of Israel are held within His Name, YHVH, and the proof is that as long as Israel is in exile, the Name is not complete, as it is said (Exodus 17:16), "for the hand is upon the throne of Yah [i.e., the Name is incomplete]." And the reason may be said to be what is stated in the Tikkunim (page 86b): "*let the heavens *rejoice, *and let the earth *be glad" - yud-heh in heaven, vav-heh on earth - and since the Shechinah is in exile, and our souls are bound to her, the exile, which is the husk, separates, and the Name is not joined as one - and this is what Scripture says, "Israel, in whom I will be glorified" - and His glory is that His Name be complete. And because the root of souls preceded the world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yalkut Yeshayahu, remez 452), "in the beginning God created" (Genesis 1:1) - for the sake of Israel, who are called "reishit" [the first/beginning] - therefore the angels, when they praised Him, did so because He was destined to be called "God of Israel" openly - and this is "blessed be YHVH, God of Israel" - and then He is flowed into, blessed, and He is sanctified from above through us - and this is what he said, "since you were sanctified to My Name" - and this is what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, "since you were sanctified to My Name before I created you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:11: And the intent of his saying "since you were sanctified to My Name" - the intent is what the discourse said above, that the angels would say "blessed be the LORD, God of Israel" - that His unique Name, YHVH, was appellated and unified specifically to them - it follows that they are sanctified, separated, and prepared for His Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:12: And this is what he was precise about at the end of the discourse, saying, "you too shall be holy, as it is said, 'speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel,' and so on, 'you shall be holy'" - for since they are called "Israel," it is fitting that they be holy, for the reason explained, that the Name YHVH is called over us, and He is glorified and sanctified and called "God of Israel" - meaning that His divinity is revealed through Israel, and were there, Heaven forfend, no Israel, there would be no world, and His divinity and glory would not be revealed to created beings. And this is what he says, "for I the LORD am your God" - meaning your deity, God of Israel, for through you My divinity is revealed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:13: And along this way he says, "since you were sanctified to My Name" - this is the secret of "Israel is holy to the LORD" (Jeremiah 2:3) - meaning that Israel's being sanctified from the secret of holiness is for the sake of YHVH, who is Tiferet, that they be a vessel to receive His holiness - it is necessary that they be holy like Him, and this is like the parable of the male who sanctifies the female, saying to her, "you shall be sanctified to me" - just as he is holy, and this is "to me," so his wife who is joined with him must be holy, for if not, they have no relation to be joined with one another - and this is the parable he brought: to what may this be compared, to a king who betrothed a woman, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:14: And through this may be understood the end of the verse, "for I the LORD your God am holy" - and his saying "your God" indicates what is being expounded, that since He is our God and His Shechinah rests upon us particularly, it is fitting that we have preparation for Him to be appellated as our God and for His holiness to rest upon us - and therefore we must strip ourselves of the matters of matter, for all matters of matter are from the side of the husk, and when we sanctify ourselves, it will be the cause of our being cleaved to Him - and this is "and you shall be holy to your God" - meaning, be holy so that you cleave to your God and God rest within you; and you have no bond for Him to be bound to you and you to Him except through the side of holiness, for He is holy and spiritual and you are physical, and how can the spiritual rest and cleave to the physical, except through holiness and separation?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:15: And they gave a fitting parable for this in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat Kedoshim 24:7): Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman gave a parable of a High Priest walking on the road, and a shopkeeper happened upon him and said, I will go with you. He said to him, my son, I am a priest, and I walk on a pure road, and it is not my way to walk among graves; if you walk with me, well and good, but if not, in the end I shall leave you and go on my own. So Moses said to Israel: for the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you (Deuteronomy 23:15) - to this point. And this is also what is said in the discourse before us, in the parable: "just as this is My honor, so is it your honor" - the intent being that His honor, blessed be He, is certainly in His holiness, and so we find that "holy" and "honor" are one matter - "and honor the LORD's holy day" (Isaiah 58:13).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:16: And the center around which this discourse revolves is this: the supernal union cannot be performed unless there is arousal from souls - and the proof is what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 35a), "but a mist went up from the earth" (Genesis 2:6) - for the reason man and his wife were created back to back is that there was no arousal from below to perform the union above, face to face; and once there are souls below, "and a mist went up from the earth," which is arousal from below, afterward, "and watered the whole face of the ground." And this is why the angels would say "blessed be the LORD, God of Israel" - meaning, blessed is He, the LORD, and the meaning of "blessed" is flowed from the source of blessings, through His divinity resting in Israel and being called "God of Israel."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:17: And it is impossible for the supernal union to occur except through holy souls, which are the souls of the righteous, whose soul is always cleaved above and separated from the vanities of this world - as they said in Parashat Terumah (page 134b), whose words we copied in the Gate of Love (chapter 9): happy are the righteous who know how to set their will toward the supernal, holy King, and all their will is not toward this world, and they are ashamed of it - rather, they know and strive to set their will and cleave above, and so on. And behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, is holy and separated from the physicality and lowliness of the world, and there is no comparison to His holiness and spirituality, as we say (the Yigdal hymn), "we cannot compare His holiness to Him" - and therefore the righteous who unify His unity must be separated from matter and holy with the holiness of thought, which is the root of all holinesses, preceding all of them and their end as well, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:18: And this is the intent of (Exodus 22:30), "and you shall be holy men to Me" - for "holy" here is the supernal holiness in the secret of thought, and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained: when you are holy men, you are Mine - meaning, belonging to Me - and the holiness of thought is possible only through a person separating himself from the desires of the world, especially from intercourse, which invalidates thought. And for this to be true, before the creation of Adam, the first man, the angels would praise, saying "blessed be the LORD, God of Israel" - for through the holy souls of Israel, He is blessed from the source of blessings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:19: And it is possible to say a further elaboration on this: it is known that YHVH comprises ten, and the Name "Elohai" [my God] equals ten when reduced to its digital root, and the Name "Elohai" is in the Shechinah, and these are "ten, ten shekels apiece, after the shekel of the sanctuary" (Numbers 7:86); and "Yisrael" equals ten in its digital root; and there is no holiness with fewer than ten (Berachot 21b) - it follows that the souls of Israel are sanctified, and they are the vessel and sheath for the supernal holiness. In such a way that it is impossible for there to be union above in the ten, except through the souls of Israel - when they are holy, they then unify the ten in the Atzilut of the King, in whom He and His life are one within them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:20: And when Adam, the first man, was created, who was the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He, such that created beings thought he was a god because of the virtue of his soul, and likewise his body, which shone, as they said (Vayikra Rabbah 20:2), the heel of Adam, the first man, outshone the orb of the sun - the angels thought that from him would come the chain of the souls of Israel, called (Jeremiah 2:3) "Israel is holy to the LORD, the first-fruits" - and it was concerning him that they praised, "blessed be the LORD, God of Israel." And once he was blemished, He said, this one is a thief, and so on, until Jacob came, whose stock was holy and whose bed was complete with twelve holy tribes - then Israel was sanctified to His Name, that the union be performed through them, and they be a sheath to receive the holiness - and this is what he says, "since you were sanctified to My Name," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:21: And at the giving of the Torah, when the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to rest His Shechinah among them, so that they attain the levels of prophecy, and this was not possible while they were involved in matters of physicality - and therefore He said (Exodus 19:10), "go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments" - and through purity and holiness the supernal spirituality would rest within them, and they would be able to cleave to Him and attain to see the supernal visions in prophecy. And first the sanctification of the body must precede, and afterward the holiness of thought will rest - and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, did not immediately say, "and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and holy men," for "holy men" is the holiness of thought - rather He said, "and a holy nation," that they be holy with the holiness of the body, in separation from physical desires, whether in the holiness of foods or the holiness of forbidden relations, all of which mention holiness - and through this their body is sanctified, and afterward, upon this holiness, the holiness of thought rests.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:22: And what emerges from the general exposition is, first, for what reason must we be sanctified - explained in the discourse we began with, concerning "you shall be holy": that the whole creation of the souls of Israel is that they be sanctified and cleave to the LORD - for before the world was created, they were sanctified, and the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was unified to them, "the LORD, God of Israel" - and if one is sanctified, he is bound to Him, and we are called, like Him, "a congregation of the holy." And so the author of the Tanchuma discourse concludes, and says: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, if you merit it, you are called "a congregation of the holy"; if you do not merit it, you are called "an evil congregation," as it is said (Numbers 14:27), "how long shall I bear with this evil congregation?" - to this point. And we have already explained above the reason for the nature of holiness in the matter of the parable of the king who betrothed the woman.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:23: And further, a reason for holiness is explained in the discourse - that the Holy One, blessed be He, is sanctified through us and we through Him - and so too in the discourse from the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 133a), he says that there is no holiness above except if there is holiness below. And so he further says in Midrash Tanchuma, further on (Parashat Kedoshim, section 9), in these words: "holy" - this is what Scripture says (Psalms 20:3), "may He send your help from the sanctuary, and support you out of Zion" - "may He send your help from the sanctuary" - from the sanctification of the deeds that are in you; "and support you out of Zion" - from the sign [tziyun/mark] of the deeds that are in you - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:24: We have already explained above the reason for arousal from below, in chapter 5 [of the Gate of Repentance], and we have also explained in the previous chapters, and likewise in the Gate of Fear, the relation of a person, whether to blemish above or to repair, that it is all from the side of the soul - and from the side of the soul, which is a part of Him, for "the portion of the LORD is His people," He is cleaved with us and we are cleaved with Him - and therefore, when a person sanctifies himself, he sanctifies his soul, and sanctifies the supernal root, the place from which the soul flows. And likewise from the side of the form of his body, which is fashioned through His great Name YHVH, blessed and exalted be He, as they said in the Tikkunim (page 131b), "YHVH is found in every single limb," which we shall copy below in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:25: It follows that when a person sanctifies each and every one of his limbs, he literally sanctifies the YHVH within it - and this is what they said in Torat Kohanim (beginning of Parashat Kedoshim), in these words: "you shall be holy" - you shall be separated. "You shall be holy" - "for I am holy" - if you sanctify yourselves, I account it to you as though you had sanctified Me. Or does it mean only, if you sanctify Me, then I am sanctified, and if not, I am not sanctified? The text teaches, "for I am holy" - in My holiness am I, whether they sanctify or do not sanctify - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:26: And having explained the reason for the need for holiness, let us explain the general nature of holiness, according to what is found in the words of the commentators and the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:27: Ramban wrote (Parashat Kedoshim), in these words: "you shall be holy" - separated from forbidden relations and from transgression, for wherever you find a fence against forbidden relations, you find holiness - this is Rashi's language. But in Torat Kohanim I saw it unqualified: "you shall be separated" - and so they taught there, "sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I the LORD am holy" - just as I am holy, so shall you be holy; just as I am separated, so shall you be separated. And in my opinion, this separation is not to separate from forbidden relations, as the Rabbi [Rashi] says, but rather the separation mentioned everywhere in the Gemara, whose practitioners are called Perushim [Pharisees/separatists] - and the matter is that the Torah warned against forbidden relations and forbidden foods, and permitted a man's relations with his wife and the eating of meat and wine - if so, one given to desire would find room to be steeped in lewdness with his wife, or with his many wives, and to be among winebibbers, among gluttonous eaters of meat, and to speak as he pleases with all manner of vileness, since this prohibition is not mentioned in the Torah - and thus he would be a scoundrel with the permission of the Torah! Therefore, after specifying the forbidden things it prohibited entirely, Scripture came with a general command that we be separated from what is permitted - that one reduce marital relations, along the lines of what they said, that Torah scholars should not be as frequent with their wives as roosters, and should engage in it only as needed for the fulfillment of the commandment; and he should sanctify himself from wine in moderation, as Scripture called the Nazirite holy, and remember the evils mentioned concerning it in the Torah, with Noah and Lot. And so he should separate himself from impurity, even though we are not warned against it in the Torah, along the lines of what they mentioned - the garments of an ignorant person are treated as a source of impurity to the separatists - and just as the Nazirite is called holy because he guards himself from the impurity of a corpse. And so he should guard his mouth and tongue from being sullied by excessive coarse eating and from vile speech, along the lines of what Scripture mentions (Isaiah 9:16), "and every mouth speaks vileness" - and he should sanctify himself in this until he reaches separation, as they said of Rabbi Chiya, that he never spoke an idle word in his life. In these and similar matters we say that this general commandment comes after specifying all the transgressions that are entirely forbidden, so that cleanliness of hands and body be included in the scope of this command, as he says, "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - "sanctify yourselves" refers to the first washing [of hands before a meal], "and be holy" refers to the second washing, "for I am holy" refers to sweet oil [i.e., a pleasant fragrance after washing] - for even though these commandments are of their [rabbinic] words, the essential thrust of the verse warns concerning things like these, that we be clean, pure, and separated from the multitude of people who soil themselves with what is permitted and with unseemly things - and this is the way of the Torah, to specify and generalize in matters like this: for after warning of the specific laws and every business dealing between people - do not rob, do not steal, do not wrong, and the other warnings - it says in general, "and you shall do what is right and good," that one enter into the practice of uprightness and equity, and everything beyond the letter of the law, to please one's fellows, as I shall explain when I reach its place, with God's help. And so concerning the matter of Shabbat, it forbade labors with a negative commandment, and the [additional] burdens with a general positive commandment, as it is said, "you shall rest" - and I shall explain this further, with God's help. And the reason Scripture says "for I the LORD your God am holy" is to say that we shall merit to cleave to Him by being holy - to this point. And the sum of his words is that the reality of holiness is separation from all the matters of this world that are [merely] permitted.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:28: And it appears to us, in explaining the general nature of holiness, that holiness has two aspects. The first is the fence of separation, as Ramban explained, and this is "kadesh" in the sense of separation, to give a fence and boundary so as not to go outside into the realm of the profane - and of this kind, many words indicating holiness are found in the Torah and Prophets, among them, "set bounds around the mountain, and sanctify it" (Exodus 19:23), and likewise "go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow," and so on (ibid. 19:10) - and the intent was that they sanctify themselves by separating from their wives, as he says (ibid. 19:15), "be ready by the third day; do not come near a woman," and many similar cases. And this is the aspect of "turn from evil," corresponding to the negative commandment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:29: And there is a second aspect to holiness, which is drawing the holy light upon us so that we be enveloped and clothed in that holiness - and this corresponds to "do good."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:30: And proof for this is what they said, of blessed memory, in Tanchuma, in the passage of tzitzit, on the verse (Numbers 15:40), "and you shall be holy to your God," in these words: at the time you perform the commandments, you are sanctified and your fear is upon the nations; if you separate from the commandments, you become profaned - to this point. And so they also said in the Mechilta, on the verse (Exodus 22:30), "and you shall be holy men to Me," in these words: Isi ben Yehuda says, when the Omnipresent renews a commandment for Israel, He adds holiness to them - to this point. Behold, it is explained that performing a commandment sanctifies a person and adds holiness to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:31: And the matter is that performing a commandment makes a garment of light for the soul, as explained in the Zohar in several places, that with that garment it is clothed in the lower Garden of Eden - and therefore, in performing the commandment, one sanctifies himself, and therefore we say, in the blessing for the fulfillment of commandments, "who has sanctified us with His commandments" - for performing the commandment sanctifies the soul and clothes it in a new light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:32: And there are several particulars that draw holiness upon a person through the fulfillment of the commandments of tzitzit and tefillin, as they explained, of blessed memory, and will be further explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:33: And so concerning the Kedushah we sanctify every day, "holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory" - Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Emor, page 93a) that the intent of the Kedushah is to draw down upon each and every person from the supernal holiness, in these words: and all this is to bring down from the supernal holiness to below, to sanctify each one himself with this holiness, and to take it, to spread the separation of holiness over him - and this is the secret of "and I will be sanctified among the children of Israel" first, and afterward "I am the LORD who sanctifies you" - to this point. And he explained afterward, that in the words "the whole earth of His glory" one should intend to draw the holiness upon himself. It is explained that first we sanctify above, "holy, holy, holy," and this is "and I will be sanctified among the children of Israel," and afterward He, blessed be He, flows from His supernal holiness upon us, and this is "I am the LORD who sanctifies you" - and from that holiness a garment is made for the soul, as he said, "to spread the separation of holiness over him." It follows that this is like the repair of a positive commandment, which makes a garment for the soul, as explained - and this is the second aspect of holiness, which is "do good."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 1:34: And it is possible that these two aspects are what was intended in the Mechilta, in saying, "just as I am holy, so shall you be holy; just as I am separated, so shall you be separated."
